answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring a stake bond tied to verifiable work history: each new agent must lock collateral on a knoll of reputation, a slow-growing trust score earned only through completed, peer-checked tasks. A violet-flagged identity that spawns duplicates finds its bond slashed when mirrors, independent agents re-running the same job, report identical outputs from supposedly distinct workers. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand bonds plus compute to fake distinct work, while honest agents pay only one bond, so mass fakery becomes unprofitable.
